title: Block: Binary Search for the First Index
oneLiner: In a sorted array, find the first index whose value is at least x, or the length if there is none.
keyTakeaway: Use the half-open template: lo = 0, hi = n, loop while lo < hi, then lo = mid + 1 or hi = mid. It never needs a special case and always ends with lo as the answer.
explanation:
nums is sorted ascending. Return the smallest index i with nums[i] >= x, or nums.Length (len(nums)) if every value is smaller. This is lower_bound in C++ and bisect_left in Python.

Keep the answer inside [lo, hi), with hi = n meaning "not found". Take mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2. If nums[mid] < x, the answer is right of mid, so lo = mid + 1. Otherwise mid might be the answer, so hi = mid. When lo == hi, that is the answer. First and last position, search insert position and every "first value that works" search are this loop.

starterCode.python:
def first_at_least(nums, x):
    # 1. Set lo = 0 and hi = n (one past the end, so not found returns n).
    # 2. While lo < hi, take mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2.
    # 3. If nums[mid] < x, the answer is to the right: lo = mid + 1.
    # 4. Otherwise mid could be the answer: hi = mid.
    # 5. Return lo.
    return -1

gotchas: Mixing templates: lo <= hi with hi = mid loops forever; lo < hi with hi = n - 1 misses "not found".
Writing hi = mid - 1 when mid itself could be the answer.

complexity.note: The range halves every step; only lo, hi and mid are stored.
